simulation_brief.endpoint_pressure: binary source-specific adjudication by NOAA/NCEI annual global report
simulation_brief.primary_decision_rule: Resolve yes only if NOAA/NCEI ranks 2025 as warmest year since records began; any lower rank resolves no.
simulation_brief.summary: A resolution-focused simulation about whether NOAA/NCEI will rank calendar year 2025 as the warmest year in the global instrumental record. T0 occurs with evidence that 2025 has been very warm globally, but prior two years were also exceptionally warm, leaving final annual ranking uncertain until NOAA/NCEI's annual global land/ocean temperature analysis is issued.
uncertainty_notes: Full-year ranking not yet fixed at T0.
Recent years provide strong competition for top rank.
Scenario corpus is sparse and does not provide numerical anomalies or publication date certainty beyond source dates.

sociology_baseline.evidence: Sparse evidence and source-specific rules encourage modest updating rather than extreme certainty.
Scenario is adjudicative and scientific, not mass-mobilization oriented.
Most of the public is low-attention and unlikely to express strong views.
Experts and forecasters cluster around shared data sources and methods.
Belief that 2025 is warmest may spread through repeated headlines, but official source can interrupt this.
Corpus emphasizes technical adjudication more than identity conflict.
Attention likely spikes near official release and fades otherwise.

sociology_prompt_influences.description: Only NOAA/NCEI annual global report determines formal resolution.
Exceptionally warm recent years make top-rank competition tight.
Very warm conditions can produce public overinference before official rank is published.
Final annual ranking requires completed year analysis, not partial or regional signals.
